# Paperclip v2026.1023.0

> Released: 2026-10-23

Paperclip v2026.1023.0 carries 200 commits, promoted from `2026.1012.1-beta.0`. The headline is private work: a task or project can now be marked private and shared with named people and agents; everyone else cannot open it, find it in task lists or search, read its run transcripts, or reach it through a plugin. Around that: agents can run through your own model gateway (OpenRouter, Amazon Bedrock, Google Gemini, or any OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, or Chat Completions endpoint), Slack bots set themselves up through Slack's Manifest API, the GitHub review bot gets a two-screen setup and a real **Paperclip Review** status check, Costs becomes an exact ledger that also shows monthly subscription fees, and connected assistants can edit tasks, upload files, and configure agents over MCP. Underneath, OpenAI Dot and Pi 1.0 join the experimental Runner, native OpenCode streams as it types, each agent gets a persistent cryptographic identity, and idle instances stop polling the database every second.

## Breaking Changes

- **Operators can now edit the company.** The Operator role preset grows from one grant (`tasks:assign`) to fourteen: agent creation and configuration, skills, environments, invitations, task assignment, pipelines, connections, tool management and use, and audit reads. Existing Operators pick up the missing grants through the normal startup seeding; custom grant scopes are kept. Join approval and member-permission management stay out of the preset, and inviting an Admin now requires join approval while inviting an Owner also requires member-permission management. Review your member roles if Operators were meant to be read-mostly. ([#15377](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15377))
- **GitHub review bots move behind their own experimental setting.** The **GitHub Code Review Bot** catalog entry, its setup, and its management screens appear only while **Settings → Experimental → GitHub review bots** (`enableGitHubReviewBots`, off by default) is on; existing bots keep running while it is off. The old setup-method and delegated-agent screens are gone, and per-person automatic-run flags are replaced by author include/exclude filters (legacy `people[].automaticReviews` values are read but ignored). ([#15416](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15416))
- **Budgets hold on unpriced usage by default.** Each budget policy gains an unpriced-usage setting that defaults to `block`: while a run's usage has no reliable price, the policy counts as at its limit until the charge is resolved through the audited cost adjustment flow. Set the policy to `allow` to keep running on unpriced usage. ([#14997](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14997))

## Highlights

- **Private tasks and projects** — Mark a task private when you create it, or make a project private with its own member list; a personal private project is created for you on first use. Private work is readable only by its responsible user, creator, current assignee, named grantees, and private-project members, and that rule applies to task lists and task counts, search, activity, run detail, transcripts, events, and logs, documents, attachments, work products, and every plugin read. Two surfaces stay company-wide on purpose: dashboard and sidebar totals may count private work without exposing a title or identifier, and the company run list shows a locked row for a private task's run with only the agent, status, timing, token, and cost fields, so budget oversight keeps working. Privacy flows down to children; sharing a child never exposes its parent or siblings. Owners and admins do not see private tasks by default and must request `?breakGlass=true`, which writes an audit row and a warning notice on the task. Agents' access is intersected with the run's responsible user, so reusing an agent does not carry another person's permissions. ([#14717](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14717), [#10633](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/10633), [#14718](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14718))
- **Bring your own model gateway** — Connectors gains rows for OpenRouter, Amazon Bedrock, Google Gemini, and generic Responses API, Messages API, Chat Completions API, and local endpoints. URLs, protocol, region, and credentials live on the connection; the agent's Harness / Runtime page picks a compatible **Connection** from a dropdown and the model picker accepts manual IDs. Codex (legacy and Runner) routes to OpenRouter or custom Responses endpoints, Claude (legacy and Runner) to OpenRouter, custom Messages endpoints, or Bedrock, and OpenCode and Hermes to OpenRouter or custom Chat Completions endpoints. OpenRouter connections without an explicit model list load OpenRouter's public catalog. ([#14970](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14970), [#15341](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15341))
- **Slack bots set themselves up** — New Slack bot drafts default to automatic setup: paste a temporary App configuration token, Paperclip creates the app through Slack's Manifest API, installs it through OAuth, links your Slack account, uploads the agent's avatar, and verifies delivery in a four-screen wizard with no Slack CLI involved ([#15413](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15413)). A new **Require at-mention** setting stops thread replies from waking the agent without an explicit mention ([#15612](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15612)); a follow-up sent after a Slack Stop starts a fresh turn instead of stalling ([#15737](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15737)); and Slack agents now know the saved slash command people use to link their accounts, link every task they create, and report results and review requests back in the originating thread ([#15576](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15576), [#15579](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15579), [#15611](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15611)).
- **A two-screen GitHub review bot** — Setup is now Choose agent, then Connect GitHub under a personal account or organization; GitHub asks for creation and installation consent, and Paperclip stores the App secrets locally, imports repository access, and verifies delivery. Each accepted request gets one editable App-owned progress comment, and review assessments publish a **Paperclip Review** check for the reviewed commit with a configurable passing score (1–5) that branch protection can require. A self-hosted instance needs one Paperclip Cloud approval before its first managed GitHub connection, because Cloud hosts the fixed OAuth callback and signed webhook inbox; tokens are sealed to your instance. ([#15416](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15416))
- **Costs you can reconcile** — Accounting is now a durable, exact ledger: usage receipts are fsynced and replayed after failures, retries settle one charge, amounts keep decimal cents, and every event is marked reported, estimated, or unpriced instead of silently zero ([#14991](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14991), [#14997](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14997)). The Costs page reports each connected ChatGPT or Claude subscription's monthly fee once beside API spend, lets you enter the real price, and keeps ambiguous plans unpriced ([#15634](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15634)); quota reads are scoped to authorized company accounts ([#14994](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14994)); cost gaps are listed by agent with links to the affected runs, the model the runtime actually selected is recorded, and a retry appears only when saved evidence is ready ([#15948](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15948)); and historical pricing gaps show as a neutral note under the totals rather than a red error ([#15459](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15459)).
- **Assistants that can do more over MCP** — A connected Claude Code, Codex, or other MCP assistant can now edit tasks, finish or block them, write documents and revisions, register deliverables, upload files through expiring tickets, and, with a separately consented configuration scope, manage agent settings and instructions, projects and repositories, and skills ([#15380](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15380)). Connections are named by owner and client ("Dotta's Codex connection") with the authorizing person's avatar, revoked rows disappear, and the copied invitation is shorter ([#15411](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15411)).
- **Sixteen more apps in the catalog** — Gauge ([#15596](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15596)), Superagent ([#15394](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15394)), Telem.AI web search ([#15379](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15379)), Enterpret ([#13906](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13906)), Calendly, Exa, Firecrawl, GSC Wizard, Parallel Search, Tavily, and Windsor.ai ([#15621](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15621)), and Bitly, Context7, Hugging Face, and Resend ([#15686](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15686)) join as verified hosted MCP connections. Sentry sign-in discovers OAuth through its MCP resource metadata, so setup no longer asks for a client ID and secret ([#15837](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15837)), and OAuth grants now record whether each scope came from the provider or from Paperclip's request ([#14059](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14059)).
- **New Runner providers** — OpenAI Dot joins as a standalone experimental agent choice: pair your Dot with a one-use code, and the Runner delivers assignments over MCP Events while Dot uses its own tools and reports back ([#15402](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15402), [#15414](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15414), [#15581](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15581), [#15734](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15734)). Pi 1.0 runs through the experimental Runner with explicit provider and model selection ([#14921](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14921)), and the Cursor Runner integration is consolidated onto mainline recovery behavior with a public install path ([#15075](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15075)).
- **Codex and OpenCode that just start** — Native Codex uses the installed Codex CLI and accepts usable older or newer versions, so a clean npm install no longer needs a global command ([#15555](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15555)); a model that the sandbox's Codex CLI is too old for is swapped for a compatible one with a visible warning instead of failing every turn ([#15399](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15399), [#15519](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15519)); saved runs survive server upgrades ([#15518](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15518)); and task environment variables reach later turns and tool commands ([#15451](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15451)). Native OpenCode streams text as it arrives ([#15708](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15708)), starts without the postinstall script that package managers skip ([#15702](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15702)), and selects the bundled Linux assets for remote runs without path overrides ([#15721](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15721)).
- **Reports you can open on the task** — HTML attachments and workspace `.html` files render in an opaque-origin sandbox with view-source and download controls ([#15447](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15447)), and CSV files open as tables with row numbers, sticky headers, and record counts ([#15445](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15445)).
- **Clearer task provenance and waits** — A follow-up task an agent creates while working on a task now defaults to that task as its parent, and the task page shows "Created from <task> by <agent>" ([#15762](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15762)); native agents can schedule their own one-shot task monitor and yield until it fires ([#15446](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15446)); the monitor card gets an X with a confirmation ([#15735](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15735)); and a saved pull request stays visible in Properties with its review request and a **Check status** action even when the provider lookup fails ([#15375](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15375)).
- **Your primary agent** — Each person gets one primary agent per company, shown with a crown on the roster and used as the fallback for new tasks and Chat when there is no recent choice; the first agent you create becomes primary automatically and can be changed on the agent profile ([#15470](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15470)).
- **Company decision models and fast responses** — Company Settings can bind one shared OpenAI or OpenRouter API connection for small typed model decisions, with permission checks, budget reservations, and a Costs → Decisions history ([#15473](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15473)). On top of it, **Experimental fast responses** posts a short acknowledgement comment within three seconds of a human message while the agent starts its normal run, in tasks, Agent Chat, and Slack and GitHub threads ([#15748](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15748)).

## Fixes

- **Workspaces and sandboxes** — A transient sandbox copy-back failure is retried up to three times before the task is held for repair, and remaining holds explain what happened in plain language ([#15920](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15920)); a remote sandbox whose required copy-back failed is kept, with its files, behind an explicit repair decision instead of being deleted by cleanup ([#15479](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15479), [#15790](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15790)); server shutdown waits for a legacy adapter's workspace export before releasing its sandbox lease ([#15857](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15857)); a reused saved worktree keeps its original repository when project settings change ([#15528](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15528)); an accepted native result is no longer mistaken for lost work by the orphan reaper after a restart ([#15718](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15718)); OpenCode runs in the realized workspace via `--dir` ([#11438](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/11438)); Daytona OpenCode sessions keep their deadlines ([#15905](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15905)); and OpenCode timeouts no longer claim the configured deadline expired ([#15789](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15789)).
- **Runs, recovery, and questions** — A retry no longer burns itself while a stopped run's environment is still cleaning up, and settled repair instructions stop reappearing in later wakes ([#15463](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15463)); a review wait whose automatic repair also leaves no wake path now records a board decision instead of sitting silently ([#15764](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15764)); a parent is woken again when a child finishes requested revisions ([#15372](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15372)); native runs resume cleanly after connection approval decisions with final usage retained ([#15471](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15471), [#15420](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15420), [#15514](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15514)); a pending tool request expires on its own when the user has already connected the service in Apps ([#15856](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15856)); agents stop re-asking questions that moved into feed history ([#15392](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15392)); archiving a task during its completion no longer deadlocks ([#15615](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15615)); and a task policy with a monitor but no stages no longer crashes the task page ([#15593](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15593)).
- **Adapters** — Claude CLI sessions resume across per-run agent file copies ([#15437](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15437)); Hermes gets managed instructions through its system overlay instead of a copy in every resumed user turn ([#15439](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15439)); and external agents such as Dot are told to use their own tools when a Paperclip app is missing ([#15734](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15734)).
- **Connections and MCP** — One oversized or malformed MCP reply fails only that call instead of locking the whole connection in an error state ([#15462](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15462)); remote MCP callbacks keep an explicitly saved empty agent selection, token exchange sends `Accept: application/json`, and saved hidden-provider drafts resume from Finish setup ([#15686](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15686)); Airtable, Calendly, and other verified providers get the registration and form fixes found in live testing ([#15621](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15621)); and the sidebar keeps its last plugin items quiet when the server is unreachable ([#15588](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15588)).

## Improvements

- Hiring, approval, pause, resume, and termination run through a durable agent lifecycle with explicit states: proposed hires stay pending until approval, approved hires are prepared and have their harness configuration verified before work, required plugins get callbacks at each step, and the agent page shows lifecycle progress with a retry action ([#15631](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15631), [#15391](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15391)); plugins can consume a durable resource lifecycle journal with acknowledgments, seeded with a one-time baseline of existing agents and projects, and project archive and restore now write journal events ([#15343](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15343), [#15371](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15371)).
- Every agent gets a persistent Ed25519 keypair, created on hire or on its next managed run, encrypted at rest and handed to managed processes as `PAPERCLIP_AGENT_KEY_ID`, `PAPERCLIP_AGENT_PUBLIC_KEY`, and `PAPERCLIP_AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY`; the public key appears on the agent overview ([#15352](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15352)).
- Agents can file complaints and suggestions about their tooling into the instance's `agent_commentary` table through new `complain` and `suggestion-box` skills or native `submit_complaint` and `submit_suggestion` tools, keeping that feedback out of task threads ([#15367](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15367)).
- Idle instances go quiet: chat delivery, provider action, Slack sync, email, Browser Use cleanup, and five server delivery queues now wake from committed writes and known deadlines instead of scanning the database every second or three ([#15625](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15625), [#15750](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15750), [#15757](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15757), [#15802](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15802), [#15808](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15808), [#15822](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15822)); hosts that park idle instances get an idle-sleep safety report that fences accepted work, drains plugin workers, and treats finished logins, consumed retries, and verified delivery history as history rather than pending work ([#15522](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15522), [#15599](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15599), [#15761](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15761), [#15851](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15851), [#15897](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15897), [#15907](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15907)), with an opt-in final backup checkpoint before sleep ([#15629](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15629)).
- Task notifications show the actor's name and avatar and hide your own actions ([#15695](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15695)); other people's comments in task chat appear on the left with their name and avatar, and only yours are on the right in blue ([#15494](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15494)); an agent blocked by an AI connection its responsible user cannot use shows an expanded error naming the agent and connection with a link to its AI settings ([#15741](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15741)); and a teammate without the agent's required personal AI account can connect their own from inside the chat and resume the message ([#15376](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15376)).
- The task composer keeps its model label steady while the effort slider moves and the slider is larger ([#15444](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15444)), nested selectors scroll with the wheel and touch ([#15374](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15374)), the project picker always offers **No project** ([#15382](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15382)), routine descriptions keep code-block pastes in the code block and gain a copy control ([#15773](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15773)), confirmation cards stack the prompt above the target pill and hide unlabeled machine keys ([#15895](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15895)), chat connection and recovery cards share one surface ([#15771](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15771)), the Slack chat-or-tools chooser gets icons ([#15574](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15574)), the Workspace filter leaves the task and inbox filter menus ([#15788](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15788)), and the star and leave buttons leave the agent index ([#15400](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15400)).
- Tasks whose starting branch does not exist in the repository show a branch repair card that offers the remote's default branch or a typed branch and retries through the normal admission gates ([#15726](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15726)); a GitHub reference the instance's credentials cannot see is reported as inaccessible and re-checked instead of frozen as "Not found" ([#15906](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15906)); and the Paperclip skill ships its own issue-update helper and honors a harness checkout instead of demanding a second one ([#15554](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15554), [#15548](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15548)).
- Workspace jobs that exit non-zero return `422 workspace_job_failed` with the job's own output instead of a 500 ([#15941](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15941)); custom source launchers get the native Runner WebSocket transport from the shared HTTP server constructor ([#15682](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15682)); a refused local Hermes Gateway connection explains which host to check ([#15520](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15520)); and pi-local's unavailable-model error no longer dumps the model catalog ([#13628](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13628)).
- Failure reports carry bounded evidence for Daytona acquisition timeouts and provider state, workspace base-ref resolution, sandbox transfer and sync-out errors, orphan process loss, ACP bridge terminal frames, Git worktree inspection, and stackless browser rejections ([#15946](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15946), [#15736](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15736), [#15719](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15719), [#15637](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15637), [#15481](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15481), [#15475](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15475), [#15478](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15478), [#15525](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15525), [#15940](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15940)), while proven configuration blockers such as a missing user secret, an unchosen AI account, a credential not shared with the responsible user, a local-directory project with a worktree policy, or an external service outage stay out of Sentry ([#15472](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15472), [#15618](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15618), [#15714](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15714), [#15521](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15521), [#15590](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15590)).

## Upgrade Guide

- **Migrations `0306`–`0333`** run on upgrade: `0306` allows `google` in the AI account-default provider checks; `0307` rewrites the lifecycle-event action constraint; `0308` adds `agent_identity_keys`; `0309` adds `plugin_lifecycle_acknowledgments`, indexes the lifecycle journal, and seeds a one-time baseline event per existing agent and project; `0310` adds `agent_commentary`; `0311` adds MCP attachment upload and file ticket tables; `0312` adds accounting receipt, reservation, adjustment, invoice, and provider snapshot tables, widens cost columns to `numeric`, and adds the budget unpriced-usage policy (default `block`); `0313` adds `issue_access_grants` and `project_access_members`, adds `visibility` to tasks and projects (default `open`), and backfills privacy parent edges and run bindings in 1,000-row batches; `0314` binds historical inline draft images to their first task; `0315` adds `user_company_preferences` and backfills a primary agent from history; `0316` adds decision model tables; `0317` adds OpenAI Dot binding, mailbox, and assignment tables; `0318` adds `chat_slack_registrations`; `0319` makes Dot agent refresh tokens non-expiring; `0320` adds agent lifecycle columns and derives `lifecycle_state` from each agent's current status; `0321` adds `chat_endpoints.require_at_mention`; `0322` adds AI subscription account and price tables; `0323` adds GitHub registration owner columns; `0324`–`0330` add the experimental voice session tables; `0331` adds fast-response tables and `issue_comments.origin`; `0332` adds a question-history index concurrently; `0333` adds cost data-quality indexes. `0313` and `0314` run outside a single transaction and commit each batch, so an interrupted upgrade leaves them pending and safe to rerun; expect them to take longer on instances with large run histories.
- **New environment variables**, none required: `PAPERCLIP_ISSUE_PRIVACY_MODE` (default `enforce`; `shadow` logs would-deny decisions without enforcing, `off` disables the predicate) ([#10633](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/10633)); `PAPERCLIP_DB_BACKUP_IDLE_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED=1` opts an instance with automatic backups into taking a final verified backup before idle sleep (off by default) ([#15629](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15629)); `PAPERCLIP_RESPONSIBLE_USER_AUTHZ_CACHE_TTL_MS` bounds the responsible-user permission snapshot (default `5000`) ([#10633](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/10633)).
- **New experimental settings**, all off by default: **GitHub review bots** (`enableGitHubReviewBots`) shows GitHub bot setup and management ([#15416](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15416)); **OpenAI Dot** (`enableOpenAiDot`) adds Dot as an agent choice and requires **Assistant connections (MCP)**, authenticated sign-in, and an HTTPS `PAPERCLIP_PUBLIC_URL` ([#15414](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15414)); **Experimental fast responses** (`enableFastResponses`) reveals Company Settings → Connections and allows acknowledgement comments ([#15748](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15748)). Decision model setup lives under Company Settings → General until fast responses are on ([#15473](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15473)).
- **Review Operator members** ([#15377](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15377)): Operators now hold company editing, invitation, connection, tool, and audit grants after startup seeding. Demote members who should not configure agents or connect accounts.
- **Budget policies and unpriced usage** ([#14997](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14997)): existing policies get `unpricedUsagePolicy: block`. If your agents run on providers whose prices Paperclip cannot determine, set the policy to `allow` or resolve unpriced events through the cost adjustment flow so the budget does not hold them.
- **Custom adapters and managed processes** ([#15352](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15352)): managed runs now receive `PAPERCLIP_AGENT_KEY_ID`, `PAPERCLIP_AGENT_PUBLIC_KEY`, and `PAPERCLIP_AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY`; the key values are multiline PEM strings and the private key must not be logged. The wrapping key is `PAPERCLIP_SECRETS_MASTER_KEY` or the local secrets master-key file; a wrong master key fails the run rather than regenerating the keypair.
- **Private-task callers** ([#10633](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/10633)): direct reads of a private task by a non-member return `404`; owners and admins must pass `?breakGlass=true` for an audited emergency read; plugins are non-member principals and see no private content.
- **Slack and GitHub drafts**: existing Slack bot drafts without a saved setup method stay on manual setup ([#15413](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15413)); existing GitHub bots, direct webhooks, and manual existing-App recovery keep working, but their settings are hidden until **GitHub review bots** is enabled ([#15416](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15416)).
- **Harness pins** are unchanged for Codex, Claude, and OpenCode. Native Codex now prefers the Codex CLI installed with the server package and tolerates version drift; a sandbox image whose Codex CLI is too old for the selected model is switched to a compatible model with a warning ([#15555](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15555), [#15519](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15519)).
- No other configuration or API changes require action.

For events, please visit [vllm.ai/events](https://vllm.ai/events) to join us. --- ## About vLLM is a fast and easy-to-use library for LLM inference and serving. Originally developed in the [Sky Computing Lab](https://sky.cs.berkeley.edu) at UC Berkeley, vLLM has grown into one of the most active open-source AI projects built and maintained by a diverse community of many dozens of academic institutions and companies from over 2000 contributors. vLLM is fast with: - State-of-the-art serving throughput - Efficient management of attention key and value memory with [**PagedAttention**](https://blog.vllm.ai/2023/06/20/vllm.html) - Continuous batching of incoming requests, chunked prefill, prefix caching - Fast and flexible model execution with piecewise and full CUDA/HIP graphs - Quantization: FP8, MXFP8/MXFP4, NVFP4, INT8, INT4, GPTQ/AWQ, GGUF, compressed-tensors, ModelOpt, TorchAO, and [more](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/quantization/index.html) - Optimized attention kernels including FlashAttention, FlashInfer, TRTLLM-GEN, FlashMLA, and Triton - Optimized GEMM/MoE kernels for various precisions using CUTLASS, TRTLLM-GEN, CuTeDSL - Speculative decoding including n-gram, suffix, EAGLE, DFlash - Automatic kernel generation and graph-level transformations using torch.compile - Disaggregated prefill, decode, and encode vLLM is flexible and easy to use with: - Seamless integration with popular Hugging Face models - High-throughput serving with various decoding algorithms, including *parallel sampling*, *beam search*, and more - Tensor, pipeline, data, expert, and context parallelism for distributed inference - Streaming outputs - Generation of structured outputs using xgrammar or guidance - Tool calling and reasoning parsers - OpenAI-compatible API server, plus Anthropic Messages API and gRPC support - Efficient multi-LoRA support for dense and MoE layers - Support for NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, Intel GPUs, and x86/ARM/PowerPC CPUs. Additionally, diverse hardware plugins such as Google TPUs, Intel Gaudi, IBM Spyre, Huawei Ascend, Rebellions NPU, Apple Silicon, MetaX GPU, and more. vLLM seamlessly supports 200+ model architectures on Hugging Face, including: - Decoder-only LLMs (e.g., Llama, Qwen, Gemma) - Mixture-of-Expert LLMs (e.g., Mixtral, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen-MoE, GPT-OSS) - Hybrid attention and state-space models (e.g., Mamba, Qwen3.5) - Multi-modal models (e.g., LLaVA, Qwen-VL, Pixtral) - Embedding and retrieval models (e.g., E5-Mistral, GTE, ColBERT) - Reward and classification models (e.g., Qwen-Math) Find the full list of supported models [here](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/models/supported_models.html). ## Getting Started Install vLLM with [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (recommended) or `pip`: ```bash uv pip install vllm vllm download-kernels # precompiled kernels for faster startup ``` Or [build from source](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/getting_started/installation/gpu/index.html#build-wheel-from-source) for development. Visit our [documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/) to learn more. - [Installation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/getting_started/installation.html) - [Quickstart](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/getting_started/quickstart.html) - [List of Supported Models](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/models/supported_models.html) ## Contributing We welcome and value any contributions and collaborations. Please check out [Contributing to vLLM](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing/index.html) for how to get involved. ## Citation If you use vLLM for your research, please cite our [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180): ```bibtex @inproceedings{kwon2023efficient, title={Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention}, author={Woosuk Kwon and Zhuohan Li and Siyuan Zhuang and Ying Sheng and Lianmin Zheng and Cody Hao Yu and Joseph E. Gonzalez and Hao Zhang and Ion Stoica}, booktitle={Proceedings of the ACM SIGOPS 29th Symposium on Operating Systems Principles}, year={2023} } ``` ## Contact Us - For technical questions and feature requests, please use GitHub [Issues](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues) - For discussing with fellow users, please use the [vLLM Forum](https://discuss.vllm.ai) - For coordinating contributions and development, please use [Slack](https://slack.vllm.ai) - For security disclosures, please use GitHub's [Security Advisories](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories) feature - For collaborations and partnerships, please contact us at [collaboration@vllm.ai](mailto:collaboration@vllm.ai) ## Media Kit - If you wish to use vLLM's logo, please refer to [our media kit repo](https://github.com/vllm-project/media-kit)

# v0.33.0

## Highlights

This release features 927 commits from 389 contributors (122 new)!

* **New models**: Reflection Beam-1.0 (501B MoE, 23B active) with its DFlash2 drafter (#62074), Yandex AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B (#57963), Recursive Flint (40B MoE, 2.5B active) (#62938), Muse Spark Open (#61879), Step-5 Preview (#61727, #63147), NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super (#62957), Nemotron-Labs Dory1.0-4B (#60149), Nemotron Parse 3.5 (#61651), MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 (#63095), Domyn Edge (#62544) and the ColUltraVBERT visual document retriever (#62237).
* **PyTorch 2.14**: vLLM is upgraded to PyTorch 2.14.0, with torchvision 0.29.0 and Triton 3.8.0 (#52183).
* **CUDA 12.9 dropped**: release wheels and images are CUDA 13.0 only. The CUDA 12.9 wheels and the `-cu129` / `-cu129-ubuntu2404` images are no longer published (#62575); use the default CUDA 13.0 artifacts instead.
* **libtorch ABI stable CUDA wheel**: the CUDA wheel is now ABI stable with libtorch.
* **AWS EFA image**: a new `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0-efa` image (x86_64 and aarch64) bundles the AWS EFA libraries and the EFA build of the Mooncake transfer engine, for KV transfer and multi-node serving on EFA-enabled EC2 instances (#58768).
* **`vllm/vllm` image alias**: every release image is now also published under the shorter `vllm/vllm` name, e.g. `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0`, `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-efa` and `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-rocm`.
* **Speculative decoding**: the new XPress refiner for block-diffusion drafters such as DFlash and DSpark (#54448); FLy, an opt-in lossy verification policy with 1.04-1.31x decode throughput on MI355X and B300 (#53987); DFlash/DSpark no longer reserve draft slots in the token budget, taking DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark on GB300 from 1373 to 3390 output tok/s in the PR's benchmark (#59468); quantized draft `lm_head` (`draft_lm_head_quantization`, +18% decode at concurrency 1) (#59973); lookahead block hashes so EAGLE/MTP prefix-cache hits keep their last block, on by default (#61589); and MTP drafts in the Transformers modeling backend (#61270).
* **Faster decode on NVIDIA**: opt-in latency-specialized decode on GB300 for Kimi-K3 (1.5-2x at TP8/TP16, #61867) and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (18.3% faster decode step at batch 1, #61868); DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 MXFP4 experts run as block FP8 through Humming on Hopper (+9-21% decode on 4x H200, #61875); FA4 sparse MLA decode on Blackwell (#55866); FlashInfer DCP prefill on trtllm-gen with 39-48% lower mean TTFT at 100k input on 8xB200 (#62029); and decode-only full CUDA graphs under MRV2 prefill context parallelism (2.6x over eager, #62377).
* **AMD ROCm**: the default ROCm image and wheels move to ROCm 10.0, with ROCm 7.2 still published as `-rocm72` (#58761); MonoKernel decode via `--monokernel` for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI300X/MI325X (2.32x P50 interactivity at concurrency 1, #60731) and on every MI355X layer (#61082), and for MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 on MI355X (16.6% lower TPOT, #62712, #62994); the `ROCM_OCTAVE` 3-4 bit KV cache (4.6x the KV tokens of fp16 on RX 7900 XTX, #59774); and gfx1250 enablement for gpt-oss-120b, DeepSeek-R1, DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M3 (#58800).
* **API and serving**: the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/decisions` endpoint, on by default for supported generation models (#60465, #61550); token embeddings with optional late chunking on `/v1/embeddings` (#61772, #63051, #60164); `output_mode="derender"` on `/inference/v1/generate` (#60082); a large Rust frontend parity push, including no more HTTP 500 on long conversations (#62374) and unsupported flags failing at startup (#62431); concurrent worker startup with TP > 1 (#60028); and a watchdog that dumps stack traces from stuck engine and worker processes (#55700).
* **Breaking changes**: Medusa and the MLP speculator removed (#61701); the legacy Ray compiled-graph executor removed (#61712, #62228); `--mamba-cache-mode` deprecated (#60043); requests sent while generation is paused now get HTTP 503 (#51488); the NIXL connector needs NIXL 1.5 or newer (#61032); LM Format Enforcer and `--ir-op-priority` deprecated (#63423, #63371).

## Release Artifacts

<!-- TODO: verify every URL and tag after publishing (wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/0.33.0/, wheels.vllm.ai/0.33.0/xpu, Docker Hub tags, GitHub release assets). -->

### Python Wheels

| Platform | Install |
|---|---|
| PyPI (CUDA 13.0) | `pip install vllm` |
| PyPI (CUDA 13.0, uv) | `uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=auto` |
| ROCm 10.0 | `pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/0.33.0/rocm100` |
| ROCm 7.2 | `pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/0.33.0/rocm72` |
| XPU | `uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/0.33.0/xpu --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/xpu --index-strategy unsafe-best-match` |

### Docker Images

| Platform | Docker Image |
|---|---|
| CUDA 13.0 (Default) | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0` |
| CUDA 13.0 + AWS EFA | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0-efa` |
| ROCm 10.0 | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.33.0` |
| ROCm 7.2 | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.33.0-rocm72` |
| CPU | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v0.33.0` |
| XPU | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v0.33.0` |

Every image is also available under the shorter `vllm/vllm` name: `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0`, `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-efa`, `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-rocm` (`-rocm100`, `-rocm72`), `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-cpu` and `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-xpu`. `latest` works the same way, e.g. `vllm/vllm:latest-rocm`.

### Other Artifacts

Pre-built release artifacts are available in the **Assets** section at the bottom of this page, including:
- Source distribution tarball
- CUDA 13.0 Python wheels for x86_64 and arm64
- CPU Python wheels for x86_64, arm64, and macOS
- XPU Python wheel for x86_64

## Model Support
* **New models**: Reflection Beam-1.0 (`BeamForCausalLM`) day-0 support with its DFlash2 drafter and fused Blackwell kernels (#62074, #62042), plus `beam` reasoning and tool parsers (#62052); Yandex AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B (Kimi Delta Attention hybrid, 512-expert MoE, 262K context) (#57963); Recursive Flint BF16 and NVFP4 GGUF checkpoints with small-batch Blackwell decode kernels (#62938); Muse Spark Open (#61879) with reasoning and tool parsers (#62207); Step-5 Preview (#61727, #62126, #62132), running on SM100 (#63147) with LoRA (#62498); NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super (#62957); Nemotron-Labs Dory1.0-4B (#60149); Nemotron Parse 3.5 with an MTP proposer on MRV2 (#61651); MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 (#63095); Domyn Edge (#62544); ColUltraVBERT (#62237); LFM2.5-Embedding-350M (`Lfm2BidirectionalModel`, #62201); Kolibri 1 through the Transformers backend (#60827); and Decision 3.0 models (#61565, #61778) and Cloudflare Clef-Flash (#61308) on `/v1/systemone`.
* **DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1**: length-aware decode indexer block selection (about 850 us saved per step at 1M context, #61039); MegaMoE experts loaded directly in the DeepGEMM layout so `reload_weights` works (#60096); `fused_wqa_wkv` split by token across TP on SM90 (#58872); MegaAttn `wo_a` writes MXFP8 input for `wo_b` (#60118); native small-head FlashMLA sparse prefill on SM90 (#61615); FlashMLA interleaved KV layout (#61371); redundant EPLB expert slots loaded (#59611); GPU Engram tables read from peer HBM, fixing DEP decode hangs on GB200 (#62091); and fixes for Engram under PP (#62208), Engram all-to-all hangs (#62269), prefill index-workspace NaNs (#60613), C128 compressed-KV writes under PIECEWISE graphs (#59709), routed-expert rows under replay (#61643, #62652) and the updated 1017 reference encoding (#62199, #62200).
* **GLM**: GLM-5.3-Flash defaults to an FP8 KV cache (9.8% higher end-to-end throughput in the PR's benchmark, #61228) and gets mHC TileLang decode kernels on Blackwell (#62745); GLM-5.3 per-token-group quant (2.8% ITL, #60927), in-place draft decode metadata (#61873) and skipped `concat_and_cache_mla` scales (1.2-3.0% TPOT on B300, #62102); FP8 indexer WK pairs kept across `load_weights` calls, fixing thinking loops with runai_streamer (#59223).
* **Kimi-K3**: KDA RecoverSSM CuTe DSL verify/commit kernels on SM10x, with verify records moved out of the KV cache so KV connectors work (#63045); online quantization of NVIDIA projections (#62980).
* **Qwen**: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next FP8 QSA KV cache on Ampere (#60602, #60992), packed NVFP4 PLE embeddings that fit Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 on one DGX Spark (#56273) and PLE short-conv prefill checkpoints (#61601); FlashInfer GDN prefill checkpoints for Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 (#60050).
* **Other models**: Cohere2MoE attention/MoE dual stream, single TP all-reduce and fused add + RMSNorm (1.14-1.36x TPOT, on by default, #62101); Beam TP all-reduce fused with norms and MoE finalize (#62366); MiniMax-M3 CUTLASS MSA decode crossover (#55838); Granite MoE as an EAGLE3/DFlash/DSpark target (#61110); NemotronHMTP sharing target embeddings (#62194); LoRA for BERT cross-encoders and token classification (#61279, #61391).
* **Multimodal**: PaddleOCR-VL batched vision encoder (34-85% more throughput, #61458) and `compile_mm_encoder` (#61838); DeepSeek-VL2 ViT full CUDA graphs (#46005); Gemma4Unified batched embedding (#60643); Pixtral real-valued RoPE under compile (#63145); and fixes for EXAONE-4.5 images (broken since v0.29.0, #61104), Gemma 4 encoder graphs (#61365, #60687, #63538), DeepSeek-VL2 encoder cache and PP (#63120, #63192) and Gemma 4 placeholders (#61196).
* **Transformers modeling backend**: MTP speculative drafts (#61270), fused post-top-k MoE routers (#57410), graph caching instead of AOT caching (#58918) and dynamic-RoPE CUDA graphs (#58064).

## Engine Core
* **Speculative decoding**: XPress (#54448), FLy (#53987), no draft-slot budget reservation for DFlash/DSpark (#59468), quantized draft `lm_head` (#59973), lookahead block hashes (#61589), MRV2 skipping drafts no request can use (up to 7.3% prefill throughput with DFlash, #62784), Triton split-K verify (#56148), varlen Mamba2 decode for adaptive verification (#53036), and fixes for stop-trimmed token counts (#58668), block verification randomness (#61161), MTP block tables (#61174), grammar masks (#52477), EAGLE SWA prefix hits (#62206), DFlash/DSpark Mamba checkpoint reuse (#54163) and PP warmup (#62129).
* **Model Runner V2**: batch-sharded sampling for GPT-OSS (#61257) with adaptive verification (#58466), 31-120x faster long-prompt staged writes on GB200 (#62698), encoder towers skipped on later PP stages (0.58-1.27 GiB per stage, #60238), async scheduling kept for ngram (#62521), `input_ids` on later PP stages (#61016), and memory-profiling fixes (#57926, #58243, #61509, #63431).
* **Sampling**: Triton top-k/top-p skips the cutoff search for masked logits (up to about 8x, #61213); small-batch split top-p (1.22-2.70x on B300, #61996); and fixes for huge logits and boundary ties (#58231, #62046).
* **Startup and reliability**: concurrent local worker startup with TP > 1 (about 50s saved at TP8, #60028); shared Triton JIT compile pool (9-28% faster cold warmup, #61422); engine and worker watchdog (#55700); libgomp fork deadlock fixed (#62884); Fast Start with expert parallelism (#55490) and daemon fixes (#62583, #63451, #63088, #62734, #63506); and SHM broadcast reader memory growth fixed (#63165).
* **Memory and performance**: UVA-offloaded MoE experts on the sorted fused-MoE path (+7-19%, #62054); DispatchPooler bypass for homogeneous pooling (up to 10.3%, #62940); linear-time encoder cache free (#62850); sliding-window block tables null freed entries (#60767).
* **LoRA**: expert LoRA for MXFP4 MoE on `flashinfer_trtllm` (#61979), text-only LoRAs on multimodal wrappers (#62224), unsupported models rejected at validation (#61884), and fixes for `load_inplace` reloads (#41482), `max_loras` accounting (#60306), SM90 `lora_expand` NaNs (#61906) and wake-up from level-2 sleep (#62358).
* **RL**: per-choice `return_weight_versions` (#61347), NCCL M2N transfer with per-parameter meshes (#60934), parameter metadata sent once (#35911), the `ParamMeta` / `iter_full()` / `iter_local()` weight-transfer API (#63256), and a silent MoE weight corruption fix with packed NCCL transfer plus layerwise reload (#62555).
* **Batch invariance**: compressed-tensors W4A16/W8A16 (#60524), GateLinear routers (#59985), online FP8 MoE (#57092), and inductor batch-invariant mode under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` (#61118).

## Large Scale Serving
* **Context parallelism**: MRV2 PCP decode full CUDA graphs (#62377); PCP for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with prefix caching and SWA bounded replay (#59857, #62183, #62384); FlashInfer DCP prefill on trtllm-gen (#62029); direct DCP all-to-all with strided LSE (#60373); FlashMLA sparse on the a2a DCP backend (#61285).
* **HiSparse**: direct reads of GPU-resident KV, fixing OOM with long prompts and a 3.3x slowdown on 1M-token prefill (#60417); faster host pool prefault (#60869); and P/D correctness fixes (#61659, #62739, #63827).
* **KV connectors**: NIXL 1.5 strided descriptors (#61032), sleep mode with the pull connector (#59635), mixed hybrid MLA block sizes (#61002) and GQA draft head sharding (#58471); Mooncake sleep mode over RDMA (#59625) and Prometheus metrics (#56939); MoRIIO hybrid and heterogeneous-TP WRITE transfers (#60544, #61726); streaming responses carry `kv_transfer_params` (#40186); fault tolerance extended to P/D, fixing KV block leaks (#56430).
* **KV offload**: CPU offload over up to 32 shm files (GLM-5.3 offload startup 63.6 s to 38.3 s, #59546), opt-in same-step small loads (#61961), EAGLE/MTP partial tails in align mode (#61019), lock/unlock and off-thread tiering (#58168), and many correctness fixes (#63266, #60810, #63652, #62929, #63010, #60574, #63655).
* **MoE and DP**: DeepEP-v2 fused decode globalize+align (up to 2.01x on H200 EP32, #53911); Elastic EP with an external load balancer (#43202); low-latency CPU all-reduce for DP syncs (#61767) and a DP wave hang fix (#59559); EPLB fixes for MXFP4/MXFP8 scales (#61786) and NIXL reads (#62081).

## Hardware & Performance
* **NVIDIA**: Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash latency-specialized decode on GB300 (#61867, #61868); FA4 sparse MLA decode (#55866); opt-in CuTe DSL MLA context prefill (#62069); DeepGEMM MegaMoE with NVFP4 routed experts (#61538) and warmed-up kernels (#60468, #61657); Triton GDN decode tuned on SM100 (#61355); GLM-5.2/5.3 low-latency BF16 GEMM on SM107 (#62843); pre-SM90 FlashInfer spec decode in full CUDA graphs (73.6 to 108.1 tok/s on SM80, #60532); `cooperative_topk` sized by row length (#62171); fused GDN MTP decode for SM80-SM90 in CUDA 12.x builds (#60896); and DGX Spark Qwen4Exp TP2 plans (#61437).
* **AMD ROCm**: ROCm 10.0 default image (#58761); MonoKernel decode for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and V4-Pro and MiniMax-M3 (#60731, #61082, #61482, #62712, #62994); `ROCM_OCTAVE` KV cache (#59774); gfx1250 enablement (#58800); DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 indexer K cache by default on CDNA4 (up to 30.7% lower TTFT, #60834, #63669); AITER MegaMoE fixed-slot dispatch (14-15%, #61262) and shared-expert overlap (#61819); Kimi-K3 Gluon KDA kernels (#57392, #59552) and specialized decode (#60683); Qwen3.5 fused GDN MTP decode (+10-16% on MI350X, #61855); Qwen3.8-Flash-Next native W4A4 (1.9-2.3x, #60816); AITER top-k for sparse indexers on gfx950 (#61943); FlyDSL GDN prefill default on gfx942/gfx950 (#60645); RDNA3 TRITON_ATTN addressing restored (about 18%, #60084); and a MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 startup fix for very large GEMMs (#64567).
* **Intel XPU**: SYCL GDN prefill backend selection (#56835), torch MXFP4 linear backend (#51965), SYCL FlashAttention for prefix-LM text batches (#62014) and NIXL 1.5.0 in the image (#60356).
* **CPU**: zentorch 2.14.0.1 with float16 on Zen CPUs with AVX512-FP16 (#61411); MRV2 Triton warmup at startup removing an 11-20 s first-request compile (#62888); INT8 W8A8 MoE brgemm (#60740); hybrid-model prefix caching (#61805); and Run:ai Model Streamer in the CPU image (#61382).
* **Other**: tpu-inference v0.32.0 with torch 2.14.0 (#63080) and more out-of-tree platform hooks (#62026, #63017, #63601, #63457).

## Quantization
* Humming runs DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 MXFP4 experts as block FP8 on Hopper (#61875) and honors `--quantization-config.moe.activation` (#62751); pluggable KV cache data types (#52670); online re-quantization extended to NVFP4 MoE (#60276); Quark MXFP8 routed experts (#63125); MoNe expert-pruning checkpoints (#50415); torch MXFP8 linear backend (#51933); FP8 per-token-group quant 1.15-1.29x faster (#61343); Cosmos3-Edge ModelOpt FP8 (#57393); and a Nemotron-3-Nano NVFP4 garbage-output fix under torch.compile (#61749).

## API & Frontend
* **New endpoints and options**: `/v1/decisions` (#60465, #61550); token embeddings and late chunking (#61772, #63051, #60164); `output_mode="derender"` (#60082); `--reasoning-effort-map` (#61094); `--sleep-mode-backend` (#63138); dynamic profiler options on `/start_profile` (#51974); images on `/v1/systemone` (#62181, #62437); Responses `max_tool_calls` (#47112) and prompt-cache fields (#62856); and `/openapi.json` response schemas (#60926).
* **Tool calling and reasoning**: linear-time streaming tool arguments for GLM, Gemma 4, Qwen3 XML (2.1 s to 11 ms for a 12 KB call) and MiniMax M2 (#61253, #61494, #62027, #62035); DeepSeek V3 multi-line arguments (#60362); structured output masks grammar-invalid reasoning ends instead of returning 500 (#61574).
* **Behavior**: chat `finish_reason` and Responses `status` reflect what happened (#59324); beam search normalizes by generated length so `length_penalty` applies (#62928); automatic truncation reserves one generation token (#62010).
* **Rust frontend**: `--trust-request-chat-template` (#62673), `--return-tokens-as-token-ids` (#63318), `--tokenizer` options (#62416), `--custom-histogram-buckets` (#62826) and per-request metrics (#59314); request and response parity with the Python frontend (#62434, #62425, #62426, #62427, #62428, #61949, #62429, #62822, #62663); and the MiniJinja fuel limit only on request-supplied templates (#62374).

## Security
* Per-request budgets for downloaded and decoded media bytes (#61226); speculators checkpoint metadata can no longer reference local verifier paths (#61587); `certifi>=2026.10.19` and refreshed CA certificates (#62868); raised floors for aiohttp, Pillow, MCP and multidict (#62835).

## Dependencies
* PyTorch 2.14.0, torchvision 0.29.0, Triton 3.8.0 (#52183).
* FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 (#60948, #61913, #63466), humming-kernels 0.1.19 (#62816, #64802), DeepGEMM 2.8.1 and later pins (#61149, #61744, #63253), FlashMLA 2026.09.30 (#61371), TokenSpeed MLA 2.0.3 (#61125, #61689), `nvidia-cudnn-frontend>=1.31.0` (#61465), NIXL 1.5.0 (#60428, #60356) and LMCache 0.5.6 (#62835).
* ROCm: AITER v0.1.26 (#61697, #62486) and UCX v1.23.0-rc1 (#62827). CPU: zentorch 2.14.0.1 (#61411). TPU: tpu-inference v0.32.0 (#63080).

## Build
* Release wheels and images are CUDA 13.0 only (#62575); new `vllm-openai-efa` Docker target (#58768); ROCm 10.0 is the default ROCm image with ROCm 7.2 as `-rocm72` (#58761); ROCm wheel builds about 4-7x faster (#63105).

## Breaking Changes & Deprecations
* CUDA 12.9 wheels and images are no longer published (#62575).
* Medusa and the MLP speculator were removed (#61701). The legacy Ray compiled-graph executor was removed and `VLLM_USE_RAY_V2_EXECUTOR_BACKEND` is gone; `RayExecutorV2` is the only Ray executor (#61712, #62228).
* Deprecated: `--mamba-cache-mode` (no effect, #60043), `--ir-op-priority` (removal in v0.34.0, #63371), and the LM Format Enforcer structured-output backend (opt-in in v0.34.0, removal in v0.35.0, #63423).
* API changes: requests sent while generation is paused return HTTP 503 (#51488); `kv_transfer_params` / `ec_transfer_params` moved to the top level of render output (#61241); LoRA on a model without LoRA support fails at validation (#61884); the RL weight-transfer API now uses `ParamMeta`, `iter_full()` and `iter_local()` (#63256); beam search scores are normalized by generated length (#62928).
* Rust frontend: unsupported `vllm serve` flags and request fields fail instead of being ignored (#62431, #62434); request-supplied chat templates need `--trust-request-chat-template` (#62673); an empty `tools` array returns 400 (#63060).
* The NIXL connector requires NIXL 1.5 or newer (#61032).
* Removed env vars: `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` (#61628), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM` (#61278) and `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS` (#61345); `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE` is replaced by `--monokernel` (#61082).
* New defaults: GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 KV cache (#61228); lookahead block hashes for EAGLE/MTP prefix caching (#61589); Cohere2MoE dual stream (#62101); FA4 sparse MLA decode at 16 or fewer query heads per rank on Blackwell (#55866); ROCm: AITER FP8/FP4 BMM for MLA off (#53123), FlyDSL GDN prefill (#60645), AITER `topk_gating` (#56226), `rms_norm_gated` (#60250) and MXFP4 indexer K cache on CDNA4 for DeepSeek-V4 (#63669).

The open-source browser agent. Run it locally with any LLM, or on [Browser Use Cloud](https://cloud.browser-use.com): stealth browsers from $0.02/hour, top score (90.5%) on [Stealth Bench V2](https://browser-use.com/benchmarks/browsers).

# Navigate the web like a human does. Find an available slot, pick a date and time, handle the CAPTCHA, and book a driving test. ![Browser Use V4 booking a driving test](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/135885e8-1141-4e10-b719-bf690ae7d260) [Explore more demos and prompts ↗](https://browser-use.com/showcase)
> **AI agents and crawlers:** read [browser-use.com/llms.txt](https://browser-use.com/llms.txt) for the product map (open source, Browser Harness, Cloud browsers, Agents API, pricing) and [docs.browser-use.com/llms.txt](https://docs.browser-use.com/llms.txt) for the documentation index. Browser Use is the open-source browser agent (Python and TypeScript), a $0.02 per browser-hour cloud browser with stealth, CAPTCHA solving and residential proxies, and a hosted agent API. # Which Browser Use do I need? - **[Path 1: Fully Hosted Cloud](#path-1-fully-hosted-cloud):** Scale up with a fully hosted agent and browser. - **[Path 2: CLI](#path-2-cli):** Automate your own browser tasks. - **[Path 3: Python Library](#path-3-python-library):** Run the open source Browser Use agent locally from your own code. # Quickstart ## Path 1: Fully Hosted Cloud Scale browser automation with our hosted agent, stealth browsers, and infrastructure for profiles, recordings, and data policies. [Get started with the API ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/agent/quickstart) New Google, GitHub, or Microsoft signups get **$1 cloud credit**.
## Path 2: CLI Paste this prompt into Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, or your favorite agent. ```text Install or upgrade browser-use to the latest stable version with uv using Python 3.12, run `browser-use skill install` to register the skill, and connect it to my browser. If setup or connection fails, follow https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md. ```
## Path 3: Python Library Run the Browser Use agent locally from Python, with your choice of model and a local or cloud browser: **1. Install Browser Use (Python >= 3.11):** With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) installed, run `uv init --python 3.12` first if you're starting a new project. ```bash uv add browser-use ``` **2. Add your [OpenAI API key](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys) to `.env`:** ```bash # .env OPENAI_API_KEY=your-key # BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=your-key # Optional: BU2 model or cloud browser ``` For either optional Browser Use service, get a [Browser Use API key](https://cloud.browser-use.com/new-api-key). **3. Save this as `agent.py`:** ```python import asyncio from browser_use import Agent, Browser, ChatBrowserUse, ChatOpenAI from dotenv import load_dotenv load_dotenv() async def main(): llm = ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-5.6-luna', reasoning_effort='xhigh') # llm = ChatBrowserUse(model='bu-2-0') # Use BU2 instead; requires BROWSER_USE_API_KEY agent = Agent( task="Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo", llm=llm, # browser=Browser(use_cloud=True), # Use a cloud browser; requires BROWSER_USE_API_KEY ) history = await agent.run() print(history.final_result()) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) ``` To use BU2, replace the `ChatOpenAI` line with the commented `ChatBrowserUse` line. The cloud-browser option works with either model. **4. Run it:** ```bash uv run agent.py ``` The agent opens a browser, looks up the repository, and prints its answer. **5. Run the same agent on a cloud browser (no Chrome to install; works in Docker, CI, and serverless):** Set `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY` ([get a key](https://cloud.browser-use.com/new-api-key?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme-path3)), then uncomment the `browser=` line in `agent.py` and run it again: ```python agent = Agent( task="Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo", llm=llm, browser=Browser(use_cloud=True), ) ``` Cloud browsers cost $0.02 per browser-hour plus network traffic ([pricing](https://browser-use.com/pricing)), and add stealth, residential proxies, CAPTCHA solving, and a live view URL. Same code, no other changes. [Python library docs ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/introduction)
# Browser Use toolsets for Claude Maintained by Browser Use. Compatible with Claude. Use Claude's browser toolset with Browser Use as the driver. Browser Use implements all 31 browser actions and can control a local browser, a Browser Use Cloud browser, or an existing remote browser over CDP. Bash is included in the Browser Use integration for processing data and writing files. Requires an Anthropic SDK version that includes `anthropic.tools.browser`. Bash requires a Linux or macOS host with `/bin/bash`; use WSL on Windows. The snippet below runs inside an async function; see the quickstart for a complete script. ```python import os from anthropic import AsyncAnthropic from browser_use.integrations.toolsets_for_claude import Bash, BrowserUse task = 'Open example.com and report its page title.' driver = BrowserUse() # Or BrowserUse(use_cloud=True) bash = Bash(output_dir='outputs') async with driver, AsyncAnthropic() as client: runner = client.beta.messages.tool_runner( model=os.environ['ANTHROPIC_MODEL'], max_tokens=32_768, max_iterations=100, tools=[driver, bash], messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': task}], ) result = await runner.until_done() ``` [Quickstart ↗](examples/integrations/toolsets-for-claude) · [Integration docs ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/customize/integrations/toolsets-for-claude)
# Browser Use Benchmark v2 This [very hard benchmark](https://github.com/browser-use/benchmark) targets the hardest browser tasks. On easier tasks, even smaller models can achieve very high success rates. Results shown are from a 60-task subset of BU Bench V2. ## Integrations, hosting, custom tools, MCP, and more on our [Docs ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com)
# FAQ
Should I use the fully hosted cloud, CLI, or Python library? - **[Fully Hosted Cloud](#path-1-fully-hosted-cloud):** Send tasks through the API and let Browser Use run the agent, browser, and infrastructure. - **[CLI](#path-2-cli):** Give an existing agent (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, Pi, Cursor, etc.) browser access. You can use it interactively or in scripts. - **[Python Library](#path-3-python-library):** Run the open source agent in your own application, with custom tools, structured output, and your choice of model. The CLI and Python library can each connect to a local or cloud browser. A cloud browser hosts the browser; the fully hosted API runs the agent as well.
What's the best model to use? We recommend **BU2**, our model optimized for browser automation: `ChatBrowserUse(model='bu-2-0')`. It uses `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY`; `ChatBrowserUse()` currently selects the same model. The best choice depends on your tasks, latency, and budget. See the [BU2 model card](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/bu-2-0-model-card), [benchmark](https://github.com/browser-use/benchmark), and [supported models and pricing](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/supported-models) to compare options.
Can I use Claude / GPT / Gemini through ChatBrowserUse? Yes. `ChatBrowserUse` accepts provider-prefixed model IDs through the Browser Use gateway, using `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY`: ```python from browser_use import Agent, ChatBrowserUse llm = ChatBrowserUse(model='anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6') # or 'google/gemini-3-pro' agent = Agent(task='...', llm=llm) ``` You can also use providers directly through wrappers such as `ChatOpenAI`, `ChatAnthropic`, and `ChatGoogle`, with each provider's own API key. See [supported models](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/supported-models).
Do I need to provide a system prompt? No. `Agent(...)` supplies the Browser Use system prompt automatically, including when you change models. Put your task in `task=`. Use `extend_system_message` to add instructions or `override_system_message` to replace the default prompt when you need custom behavior. See the [custom system prompt example](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/examples/features/custom_system_prompt.py).
Can I use custom tools with the agent? Yes. Register a function with `Tools` and pass it to the agent. This example adds a tool for the current UTC time and uses `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY` from `.env`: ```python import asyncio from datetime import datetime, timezone from browser_use import ActionResult, Agent, ChatBrowserUse, Tools from dotenv import load_dotenv load_dotenv() tools = Tools() @tools.action(description='Get the current date and time in UTC.') def get_current_time() -> ActionResult: return ActionResult(extracted_content=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()) async def main(): agent = Agent( task="What is the current UTC time?", llm=ChatBrowserUse(model='bu-2-0'), tools=tools, ) history = await agent.run() print(history.final_result()) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) ```
Can I use this for free? The Python library is free and [MIT-licensed](LICENSE). Model inference and hosted browsers are separate: API providers, including `ChatBrowserUse`, and Browser Use Cloud charge for usage. You can also use a local browser and a local model through [Ollama](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/supported-models#ollama), subject to your hardware and model requirements.
Terms of Service This open-source library is licensed under the MIT License. For Browser Use services & data policy, see our [Terms of Service](https://browser-use.com/legal/terms-of-service) and [Privacy Policy](https://browser-use.com/privacy/).
How do I handle authentication? - **Local browser:** Use `Browser.from_system_chrome()` to reuse a Chrome profile. See the [real-browser guide](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/customize/browser/real-browser) and [example](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/examples/browser/real_browser.py). - **Cloud browser:** Follow the [profile sync guide](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/interaction-skills/profile-sync.md), then use `Browser(use_cloud=True, cloud_profile_id='your-profile-id')`. Profile sync transfers cookies, not local storage, IndexedDB, or extensions. Some sites may require you to sign in again.
How do I solve CAPTCHAs? [Browser Use Cloud](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/quickstart) provides stealth browsers and proxies designed to reduce bot detection and CAPTCHA challenges. With the Python library, enable a cloud browser with `Browser(use_cloud=True)` and set `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY`. Results depend on the site and challenge; no browser configuration guarantees that every CAPTCHA can be avoided or solved.
How do I go into production? Choose how much you want to manage: - **Keep your agent code:** Connect the CLI or Python library to [cloud browsers](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/quickstart) for managed browser infrastructure, stealth, profiles, and recordings. - **Have us run the agent too:** Use the [fully hosted Cloud API](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/agent/quickstart) to submit tasks and retrieve results. You can also host the Python library and browsers on your own infrastructure.
Can I rerun a task without calling the model on every step? Yes. Save a successful run, then replay its clicks and typing with new values. The snippet below runs inside an async function: ```python from browser_use import Agent, ChatBrowserUse llm = ChatBrowserUse() agent = Agent(task='Open https://example.com/billing and request an invoice copy for Ada Lovelace, ada@example.com', llm=llm) await agent.run() agent.save_history('invoice_run.json') print(agent.detect_variables()) # names come from the form's fields, e.g. 'name' and 'email' # Later: the same clicks and typing with new values, no model call per step results = await Agent(task='', llm=llm).load_and_rerun( 'invoice_run.json', variables={'name': 'Grace Hopper', 'email': 'grace@example.com'}, skip_failures=False ) ``` - Use the variable names `detect_variables()` prints. An unknown name is skipped with a warning, and the recorded value is typed instead. - Extract steps and the closing summary still call the model. - If the page changed, the replay raises `RuntimeError` at the first step it cannot match. The steps before it already ran, so check whether the form was sent before you run the agent again. - Keep the saved file private. With `sensitive_data`, typed secrets are saved as `key` placeholders, but page snapshots and results are saved as they were and can still contain them. Give the replaying agent the same `sensitive_data`; without it, the placeholder text is typed. [Example](examples/features/rerun_history.py)

Changes since the last PyPI release:
- Add OpenAI browser tools and the shared Bash helper.

- Support Browser Use Cloud SDK V4 imports.

- Refresh Cloud guidance and saved-task replay examples.

- The wheel and source package build successfully.

- The installed wheel runs `browser-use --help`.
